svg.title: Ternary and XOR/Hamming arithmetic
svg.desc: Three panels. Left: 16 ternary weights stored as two bit strips, plane P marking +1 and plane N marking -1, beside a 16-bit activation strip. An AND with the activation lights the surviving bits: 5 survive in P and 2 in N, and the dot product is 5 minus 2, which is 3. XOR is crossed out because it is not the ternary dot product. Middle: a query and two E8 root candidates drawn as bar rows over 8 coordinates. Both candidates sit at L1 displacement 3, a tie, and the count of differing coordinates, 2 against 1, breaks it in favour of the second; this is how the current discrete model selects routes. Right: a dense grid with every weight cell lit beside a routed grid with only a few cells lit. Removing the multiplier does not remove the dense sum.
svg.text: Ternary arithmetic: AND and subtract, not XOR, and the dense sum stays
A zero weight is skipped for free.
Over GF(2), −1 and +1 are the same element,
so "ternary XOR matmul" is false as stated.
2 A tie broken by a count
Equal L1, so fewer differing coordinates
Dense: every one of the W × D weights
Routed subset: only the selected cells are
Weights, activations and the query are worked examples. The AND-and-subtract identity is exact (re-checked in 5,000 random trials). Status: parked.
